newsitem.title: UK: U.S. STOCKS FIRM IN LONDON, DOW SEEN HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: U.S. STOCKS FIRM IN LONDON, DOW SEEN HIGHER.

text.p: U.S. stocks were firmer across the board in London, and dealers here were expecting the Dow to open 10 to 12 points higher after yesterday's record close.
"It's looking good. You can't seem to keep the market down at the moment," said one London dealer.
Shares in telecommunications giant AT&T Corp were up 1/8 in London to 39 ahead of the company's announcement, expected today, detailing its new expanded communications services.

Other technology shares rose after having been hit in recent sessions. Shares in International Business Machines and Compaq Computers each added 3/8 in London to 123-7/8 and 64-5/8, respectively. Shares in Digital Equipment climbed 1/8 to 35.
Automobile makers were higher after Chrysler Corp and General Motors released U.S. September vehicle sales.

Chrysler reported robust September sales, up 22 percent, while GM reported a slight drop. Disappointment with GM's sales, however, was overshadowed by optimism surrounding the upcoming launch of GM's new minivan line, brokers said.
GM shares were up 1/8 to 49-1/2 in London, while Chrysler shares gained 1/4 to 29-1/4.
Shares in Ford Motor Co were quoted at 31-3/4, up 1/8. Ford is set to release its sales tomorrow.
In trading on Globex, the December S&P 500 futures contract was 1.40 higher at 696.50 at 1026 GMT. The December 30-year Treasury bond futures contract was up 7/32 at 110-4/32.
On Tuesday, the Dow added 22.73 points, bringing it to a record 5,904.9.
